title: Yudhishthira and the Dog
text:
At the end of their lives, after the great war and many years of rule, the five Pandava brothers and their wife Draupadi gave up their kingdom and set out on a final journey toward the Himalayas, heading for the mountain of the gods. A dog joined them at the start and followed them all the way.

One by one, the travelers fell on the road and died: first Draupadi, then the twins Sahadeva and Nakula, then Arjuna, then Bhima. Yudhishthira walked on without looking back, and only the dog stayed with him.

At last the god Indra appeared in his chariot to carry Yudhishthira to heaven in his own body. Yudhishthira asked to bring the dog, which had been devoted to him. Indra refused: there was no place in heaven for dogs, and Yudhishthira should simply leave it behind. Yudhishthira said that abandoning one who was devoted to him, frightened and without other protection, was a grave sin, and he would not do it even to gain heaven.

The dog then changed shape. It was Dharma, the god of righteousness and Yudhishthira's own divine father, testing him. Praising his steadfastness, Dharma and Indra took him to heaven.
lesson: The way you treat those who depend on you, especially when you are about to move on to something better, shows what you really are. Do not trade loyalty for advancement.
